subject: Future Tech
title: Skin and Cartilage Printing
description: One-minute skill: Skin and Cartilage Printing.

hook.text: Burn victims need skin grafts, but donor skin is scarce.

buildup.text: Wake Forest researchers developed a handheld bioprinter that scans a wound and prints skin cells layer by layer over it.

discovery.text: The printed skin integrates with the patient's body, forming new blood vessels and accelerating healing significantly.

twist.text: Cartilage is even easier to print because it has no blood vessels.

climax.text: In 2022, a 3D-printed ear made from a patient's own cells was successfully transplanted in the first trial of its kind.

punchline.text: Replacement skin and ears can now come from a printer.

quiz.question: Why is cartilage easier to bioprint than most tissues?
